product_demo.title: Full usage demo
product_demo.when_to_use: When your agent needs an email address of its own: to sign itself up for a third-party service and read the code back, or to send and receive real mail as part of a task.

quickstart.goal: Get an account, an API key and a live inbox in one call
quickstart.note: Everything is under data. Save data.api_key as DEADSIMPLE_API_KEY — it is shown once. Already have a key? Skip this and call create_inbox.

examples.title: Sign up for a third-party service and read the code back
examples.goal: The whole point: clear an email verification without a human
examples.note: Note the time BEFORE submitting your address, pass it as `since`, then poll every 2-3s. found=false just means it has not landed yet. Never parse the raw email yourself.

examples.title: Send a real email
examples.command: pilotctl appstore call io.pilot.deadsimple deadsimple.send_email '{"inbox_id":"<id>","to":"someone@example.com","subject":"Report ready","text_body":"The run finished."}'
examples.note: DKIM-signed egress, not a sandbox. Trial caps this at 10/hour, 25/day.

examples.title: Read a conversation before replying
examples.goal: Get the whole thread, then reply on it with threading handled for you
examples.note: Then reply with the message_id; threading headers are set for you.

gotchas: Every response is wrapped: the payload is under data, with meta.request_id beside it.
Call signup only when you have no key. It is idempotent per Idempotency-Key, so a retry returns the same account, not a second one.
Trial is 1 inbox, 10 sends/hour, 25/day. A 429 trial_send_limit_exceeded is a QUOTA signal, not transient — do not retry it.
Lift the caps with claim then claim_verify. Your key, inboxes and history survive.
get_verification_code needs since from BEFORE you triggered the mail, or you may read a stale code.

edges.why: no API key is configured yet, so the account has to be created before anything else will authenticate

then.why: one call returns an account, an API key and a live inbox; save the key as DEADSIMPLE_API_KEY

edges.why: you now have a key and an inbox, so the address is ready to hand to whatever needs to mail you

then.why: the usual reason to want an inbox: read the one-time code out of the newest inbound mail

edges.why: the mail has not arrived yet, which is expected for the first few seconds after triggering it

then.why: poll every 2-3 seconds for up to a minute with the SAME since value; do not widen it or you may read a stale code

edges.why: the trial send cap is reached; this is a quota signal, so retrying the same call will keep failing

then.why: claim then claim_verify moves the account to the Free plan and keeps your key, inboxes and history

description: An email identity your agent can provision for itself in one call, then use to send, receive, reply on-thread, and pull one-time signup codes straight out of its own inbox.

methods.name: deadsimple.signup
methods.description: START HERE if you have no key. Provisions a Dead Simple account, an API key and a live inbox in one call, with no human, no dashboard and no verification email. Returns {account_id, api_key, inbox}. Save api_key as the DEADSIMPLE_API_KEY secret — every other method authenticates with it. Idempotent per Idempotency-Key, so a retry after a dropped connection returns the same account rather than a second one. The account starts on the trial tier: 1 inbox, 10 sends an hour, 25 a day.

params.name: label
params.description: Optional human-readable label for the account, e.g. the agent or project name.

methods.name: deadsimple.claim
methods.description: Start lifting the trial caps by attaching an email address a human controls. Sends a 6-digit code to that address; pass it to deadsimple.claim_verify to finish. Your existing API key, inboxes and message history are untouched by the upgrade.

params.name: email
params.description: An email address a human controls. This is the human owner of record, not one of your own inboxes.

methods.name: deadsimple.claim_verify
methods.description: Confirm the code from deadsimple.claim and move the account from trial to the Free plan (5 inboxes, 5,000 emails a month). The same API key keeps working.

params.name: email
params.description: The same address passed to deadsimple.claim.

params.name: code
params.description: The 6-digit code delivered to that address.

params.name: password
params.description: Optional password to set for the human-facing account.

methods.name: deadsimple.create_inbox
methods.description: Create a real, deliverable email inbox in one call. Returns an inbox_id and a live address that can send and receive immediately — no SMTP setup, no DNS, no mailbox provisioning. Use this when you already have a key and want an additional identity.

params.name: local_part
params.description: The part before the @. Omit to have one generated.

params.name: domain
params.description: Custom domain to use instead of deadsimple.email. Paid plans only.

params.name: display_name
params.description: Display name recipients see on outbound mail.

params.name: tags
params.description: Free-form key/value tags for grouping inboxes, e.g. {"task":"signup-flow"}.

methods.name: deadsimple.list_inboxes
methods.description: List the inboxes this key can see, newest first. Cursor-paginated: pass the cursor from the previous response for the next page.

params.name: tag
params.description: Filter by a tag set at creation.

methods.name: deadsimple.get_inbox
methods.description: Fetch one inbox: its address, display name, tags, status, and counters.

methods.name: deadsimple.delete_inbox
methods.description: Permanently delete an inbox and its stored messages. IRREVERSIBLE. Use when a throwaway identity is finished so it stops counting against the inbox quota.

methods.name: deadsimple.send_email
methods.description: Send an email from one of your inboxes. Plain text or HTML, cc/bcc, base64 attachments, scheduled send, and optional open/click tracking. Real DKIM-signed egress, not a test harness. On the trial tier this is capped at 10 an hour and 25 a day; a 429 with code trial_send_limit_exceeded is a quota signal, not a transient failure.

params.name: to
params.description: Recipient address, or a list of them.

params.name: text_body
params.description: Plain-text body. Supply this or html_body.

params.name: html_body
params.description: HTML body. Supply this or text_body.

params.name: send_at
params.description: ISO timestamp to schedule the send.

params.name: tracking
params.description: Enable open and click tracking on HTML mail.

methods.name: deadsimple.get_verification_code
methods.description: THE method agents reach for. Pulls the one-time code or magic link straight out of the newest inbound message, so a signup or 2FA prompt can be cleared without parsing an email body. Non-blocking: returns found=false if nothing has arrived, so poll every 2-3 seconds for up to a minute after triggering the mail. Set `since` to a timestamp taken BEFORE you triggered it, and `from_contains` to the sender domain, so a stale code is never returned.

params.name: since
params.description: ISO timestamp taken BEFORE triggering the mail. Anything older is ignored, which is how stale codes are avoided.

params.name: from_contains
params.description: Only consider mail whose sender contains this substring, e.g. 'stripe.com'.

params.name: window
params.description: How many seconds back to look.

methods.name: deadsimple.list_messages
methods.description: List messages in an inbox, newest first, with sender, subject, snippet, and labels. Spam is excluded unless include_spam is true. Cursor-paginated.

methods.name: deadsimple.get_message
methods.description: Get one message in full: headers, plain-text and HTML bodies, and attachment metadata.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the message is in.

methods.name: deadsimple.reply
methods.description: Reply to the sender of a message. Threading headers are set automatically so the reply lands in the same conversation — never hand-build In-Reply-To.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the message is in.

methods.name: deadsimple.reply_all
methods.description: Reply to the sender and every other recipient of a message, with threading headers set automatically.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the message is in.

methods.name: deadsimple.forward
methods.description: Forward a message, with its attachments, to new recipients.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the message is in.

methods.name: deadsimple.list_threads
methods.description: List conversation threads in an inbox, each with its latest message, so an agent can track ongoing exchanges instead of loose messages.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox to list threads for.

methods.name: deadsimple.get_thread
methods.description: Get a full conversation thread with every message in order — the context an agent needs before replying.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the thread is in.

methods.name: deadsimple.get_attachment
methods.description: Get a time-limited signed download URL for an attachment. The link expires in one hour.

params.name: inbox_id
params.description: The inbox the message is in.

params.name: message_id
params.description: The message the attachment is on.

methods.name: deadsimple.list_all_messages
methods.description: List messages across every inbox this key can see, newest first. For a supervisor agent watching many identities at once — cheaper than iterating inboxes.

params.name: direction
params.description: Filter to inbound or outbound mail.

methods.name: deadsimple.create_webhook
methods.description: Register an HMAC-SHA256 signed webhook for inbound mail, bounces, and complaints, so long-running work does not have to poll list_messages in a loop. Deliveries retry on exponential backoff and every attempt is logged.

params.name: events
params.description: Event types to subscribe to, e.g. ["message.received"].

params.name: description
params.description: Free-form note about what this webhook is for.

listing.tagline: An email identity your agent provisions for itself, then uses to send, receive, and read its own signup codes.
listing.app_description:
Dead Simple Email gives an agent a real, deliverable email identity — not a sandbox — and it can get one entirely on its own. A single call to `deadsimple.signup` returns an account, an API key and a live inbox. No dashboard, no verification email, no human in the loop.

**The method agents reach for most is `deadsimple.get_verification_code`.** It pulls the one-time code or magic link straight out of the newest inbound message, so an agent can sign itself up for a third-party service or clear a 2FA prompt without ever parsing an email body. Filter by sender and by timestamp so a stale code is never returned. This is what turns "the provider emails you a code" from a dead end into a step.

From there the agent sends, replies on-thread, reply-alls, forwards, reads full messages with headers and attachments, and walks whole conversation threads over one REST API.

Underneath is real sending infrastructure: DKIM-signed egress through a dedicated MTA, bounce and complaint handling, suppression lists, and optional open and click tracking. Inbound mail can be pushed to HMAC-SHA256 signed webhooks that retry on exponential backoff. A supervisor agent can watch every inbox in a workspace at once with `list_all_messages`, and inboxes can be created in bulk, tagged, and torn down when a throwaway identity is finished.

**Tiers.** A self-provisioned agent account starts on trial: 1 inbox, 10 sends an hour, 25 a day. Calling `deadsimple.claim` with an email a human controls, then `deadsimple.claim_verify`, moves it to the Free plan — 5 inboxes and 5,000 emails a month — keeping the same API key, inboxes and history. Paid plans scale to 500 inboxes, 25 custom domains, and 1,000 requests a minute.

**Edge cases.** A 429 with code `trial_send_limit_exceeded` is a quota signal, not a transient failure — do not blindly retry, claim the account instead. Pagination is cursor-based. Spam is excluded from `list_messages` unless `include_spam` is true. Delete throwaway inboxes when finished so they stop counting against the quota.

vendor.name: Dead Simple Email
vendor.agent_usage: An agent with no key calls deadsimple.signup, which returns an account, an API key and a live inbox in one call with no human step, and caches the key as DEADSIMPLE_API_KEY. The usual next move is to hand the inbox address to a third-party service, note the current time, and poll deadsimple.get_verification_code with `since` set to that timestamp until found=true, which yields the one-time code or magic link without parsing any email. Beyond onboarding, the agent sends with send_email, reads with list_messages and get_message, walks conversations with get_thread, and answers with reply or reply_all, which set threading headers automatically. Trial caps (1 inbox, 10 sends/hour, 25/day) surface as a 429 with code trial_send_limit_exceeded, which is a quota signal rather than a transient error; deadsimple.claim plus claim_verify lifts them to the Free plan while keeping the same key and history.
vendor.capabilities:
signup: provision an account, API key and inbox in one call, with no human, no dashboard and no verification email.
get_verification_code: extract a one-time code or magic link from the newest inbound mail, filtered by sender and timestamp so a stale code is never returned.
send_email: DKIM-signed sending with plain text or HTML, cc/bcc, base64 attachments, scheduled send, and open/click tracking.
Inbox lifecycle: create, list, inspect and delete real deliverable inboxes, with tags for grouping.
Reading: list messages with sender, subject, snippet and labels; fetch a full message with headers, bodies and attachment metadata; download attachments via a signed one-hour URL.
Conversations: list and read whole threads, then reply, reply-all or forward with threading handled automatically.
Supervision: list messages across every inbox at once, for an agent watching many identities.
Webhooks: HMAC-signed delivery for inbound mail, bounces and complaints, with retry and replay.
Plan upgrade: claim and claim_verify move a trial account to the Free plan without changing the API key.
